I farm 6 mu here in Quzhou, and I split it like I have for many years. Three mu I keep for cotton — that is our main crop, one season, plant in April after the ground warms, pick in October. The other 3 mu I do wheat in winter, then maize straight after in June. That way my family has grain and I still get cash from cotton.

For cotton, I use Bt hybrid seed — the bollworm used to eat us alive before, now it is manageable but I still spray maybe 7-8 times for aphids, spider mites, and late bollworm. I put down about 20 kg urea (N), 9 kg DAP for phosphorus, and 8 kg potash per mu. I know cotton eats a lot of potassium or the bolls do not fill. I plough deep in spring. Water from the well 4 times — before planting, at squaring, flowering, and boll-filling. I expect maybe 270 kg seed cotton per mu if the weather is fair.

For wheat, I sow improved variety in early October after rotary tillage. Base fertilizer plus topdressing at jointing, about 16 kg N total, 7 kg P, 5 kg K. I irrigate 3 times — winter water, returning-green, and grain-filling. Spray 2 times for aphids and rust. Expect 450 kg/mu.

For summer maize, I use hybrid seed, no-till right into the wheat stubble. 17 kg N, 6 kg P, 6 kg K. Two irrigations if the rain is poor. Two sprays for borer and armyworm. Expect 550 kg/mu.

I am 74 — I cannot work like before, so my sons help at busy times and I hire a machine for ploughing and harvest. I would rather spend a bit extra on fertilizer than lose a harvest. At my age, one bad year hurts more than wasted fertilizer.
